_comment: The source registry for NYC. One entry per source, each naming an adapter.
MVP = tier 2 only (NYC Open Data). Tier 0 aggregators (PredictHQ, SeatGeek)
and tier 1 venue adapters need keys or bespoke parsers; see coverage.md.
Datasets audited 2026-08-01. fudw-fgrp (Parks Events Listing) and
6v4b-5gp4 (Parks Special Events) are DEAD -- their newest rows are from
2019 -- and are deliberately absent rather than silently returning nothing.

sources.label: NYC Parks Public Events - Upcoming 14 Days
Squarespace venue calendars
_comment: Venue-published events, one collection per venue. The registry of
venue -> collection URL is discovered by squarespace.py and committed;
this adapter only fetches. Re-run discovery when venues redesign, not
on every run. Events live in the response's `upcoming` array -- for an
events collection `items` comes back empty, which is the whole trick.

sources.label: Luma community calendars
_comment: Organiser-led programming -- meetups, run clubs, reading and craft
groups -- which appears in no other source here. Each calendar
publishes a real ICS feed at api.lu.ma/ics/get, the Subscribe
button's own endpoint; this is a feed used as a feed, not a scrape.
Discovery is the limit, not access: there is no city-wide feed and
the /nyc page yields 20 calendars per load, so luma.py MERGES its
registry on each run and the roster grows over time.

sources.label: Ticketmaster Discovery
_comment: DMA 345 is the New York media market, which reaches Newark, Long
Island and lower Connecticut. state_code trims the other states at
the API; normalize.py then drops anything whose venue coordinates
fall outside an NYC neighbourhood polygon, which is the real test.
Sharded one day per request: deep paging caps at 1000 items and the
market holds ~4,600 events per month, so a single broad query would
silently see only a fifth of them.
Key lives in .env as TICKETMASTER_API_KEY (gitignored).
